transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: You smell like the Sidr trees. I'd forgotten that scent had a name.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Save the nostalgia. Where is the exit?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Keep your voice down. The stone houses have ears and they have patience.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm not whispering to shadows. Point me to the surface.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: There is no pointing from here. I have been by this stone rim forty years and I still don't know what's past the square.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Forty years just sitting here. You gave up.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I learned. The ones who run are the ones who scream first. This fountain is the only place the oil doesn't breach.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: So you hid. That's all you did.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I stayed alive. You can call it what you want.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Tell me about the shadows in the houses. What are they.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't point at them. They rank themselves by how close they dare sit to the center. They watch for mistakes, and yours are already showing.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Who commands them.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Lower when I say this. There is a king. Ancient, between fire and will. Everything here reports to him whether it knows it or not. That is all I will say of him — saying more is how this place punishes you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: And the girl at the gate. She just stared at me when I passed.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: She is not a guard. She is a mirror. She shows you what you want and waits to see if you reach for it. I saw someone fail that once. I won't describe after.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: What's in the black sludge. I saw hands.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: People who bargained wrong. They aren't jinn. They don't think anymore. Don't speak near the dark water — it remembers names.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: My brother is down here because of me. I dared him to insult the well and a pale hand took him before I could move.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Say the rest. Don't soften it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It was my dare. He trusted me. That's all there is.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Omar is kept, not lost. The king chose to hold him. That is worse than lost but it means he is still there to find.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then I'm going to him. Does anything work against the dark or not.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: There is a light the dark remembers fearing. When it is called, the hands sink and the watchers go quiet — just long enough to move. Saying that much already costs me.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Good. Let them hear. Give me the words.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: It is not a weapon you swing. It is a flare you spend. Use it wrong and you stand empty while the dark stays.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'll take that risk. What are the words.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: My jaw aches just reaching for it. The bubbling pool stirs when I think about saying it out loud — look, one of the windows just went dark.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then say it fast before more go dark.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: The prayer rings like a bell. Everything in the dark will know where you stand the moment it leaves your mouth.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I want them to know. I want them to fear me.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Brother... I had a — the face is gone. Doesn't matter. You're angry and still breathing. That's more than most who came down here.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Don't fade on me now. Stay with me.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I'm here. The pale hands are your first problem when you move. Use what I give you only when they reach — not before. Call it early and it burns out before the dark does.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: When the hands reach. Not before. I understand.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: One more thing. The black surface goes quiet before it takes something. That quiet is not peace — it is the well deciding.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Stop warning me and give me the words.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't answer anything that calls your brother's name in a voice that isn't his. The dark learns mouths. That rule costs you nothing to keep.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'll remember it. Now speak.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break. Say it once.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't repeat it. The square listens for echoes. There is one more thing and it costs more than the first.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Give it. All of it.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Prayer for the lost: Light find my hand. Light find my path. Let the Sword of Light answer, and let it fade when the shadows loosen. Never say it twice in the same dark.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I have both. I won't waste them.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Use the first when you feel yourself slipping. Use the second when the hands reach. The order matters.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: First to hold myself. Second when they grab. Got it.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: My hands won't stop shaking now. That's what giving it costs. The square already knows I spoke.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then I won't waste the time it bought you.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Carry one more thing out with you. Hanash, from the valley. The one who never made it home.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'll say your name where the sun can hear it. I swear it.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: You are still angry. Good. Don't let this place trade it for something quieter.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm going. For Omar.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I know. Find a better end than mine.
